entries.blurb: The Spirit is the Lord and giver of life, present at creation, empowering judges, kings, and prophets, and promised by the prophets for all God's people. At Pentecost he is poured out on the church.

entries.title: The Gifts of the Spirit
entries.blurb: The Spirit gives gifts to God's people for the good of others: teaching, serving, leading, giving, mercy, and others Paul lists in Romans 12, 1 Corinthians 12, and Ephesians 4.

entries.title: Covenant
entries.blurb: A covenant is a binding relationship sealed by promise and oath.

entries.title: The Law
entries.blurb: The law given at Sinai was God's instruction for a redeemed people, a way of life shaped by his holiness, not a ladder to earn rescue. Israel was rescued first and given the law second.

entries.title: Israel in God's Purpose
entries.blurb: God chose Israel to be his people and, through Abraham's family, to bless all nations. The New Testament wrestles with Israel's place after Christ, especially in Romans 9 to 11.

entries.title: Exile and Restoration
entries.blurb: Exile is one of the Bible's great patterns: Adam and Eve sent from the garden, Israel carried to Assyria and Babylon for breaking the covenant, and God's promise to gather and restore.

entries.title: Holiness
entries.blurb: God is holy, set apart in his purity and majesty, and he makes a people holy to belong to him.

entries.title: Tabernacle, Temple, and God's Presence

entries.title: Sabbath and Rest
entries.blurb: God rested on the seventh day and gave Israel the Sabbath as a sign of the covenant and a gift of rest, for servants, strangers, and animals as well.

entries.title: The People of God and the Church
entries.blurb: God's purpose has always been a people: Israel, called to be a light to the nations, and then the church, Jew and Gentile together in Christ, called his body, his bride, and his temple.

entries.title: Baptism and the Lord's Supper
entries.blurb: Jesus gave his church two practices: baptism, the sign of entry into Christ, and the Lord's Supper, the meal that proclaims his death until he comes.

entries.title: Leadership and Office in the Church
entries.blurb: The New Testament describes elders or overseers who shepherd and teach, deacons who serve, and a pattern of leadership modeled on Jesus, who came not to be served but to serve.

entries.title: The Nations and Mission
entries.blurb: From the promise to Abraham that all families of the earth would be blessed, God's purpose reaches every nation.

entries.title: Worship

entries.title: Love of God and Neighbor
entries.blurb: Jesus named two commandments as the greatest: to love God with all one's heart, soul, mind, and strength, and to love one's neighbor as oneself.

entries.title: Prayer and Lament
entries.blurb: Prayer is speaking to the God who speaks. The Psalms give every kind of prayer words: praise, thanksgiving, confession, and lament that argues with God in faith.

entries.title: Wisdom
entries.blurb: Biblical wisdom is skill in living well in God's world, beginning with the fear of the LORD.

entries.title: The Fear of the LORD
entries.blurb: The fear of the LORD is reverent awe before God that shapes a whole life. Proverbs calls it the beginning of wisdom and knowledge.

entries.title: Suffering and Evil
entries.blurb: Scripture does not hide suffering. It gives whole books to it: Job, Lamentations, and many of the Psalms.

entries.title: Idolatry
entries.blurb: Idolatry is giving to anything created the trust, love, and worship that belong to God alone. In Scripture it ranges from carved images to greed, which Paul calls idolatry.

entries.title: Justice, the Poor, and the Stranger
entries.blurb: The God of the Bible defends the orphan, the widow, the poor, and the foreigner, and he requires his people to do the same.

entries.title: Money and Possessions
entries.blurb: Scripture treats wealth as a gift from God and a dangerous rival to him. It commands generosity, forbids exploitation, and warns that the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil.

entries.title: Government and the State

entries.title: The Kingdom of God
entries.blurb: The kingdom of God is his rule breaking into a rebel world to set it right. The Old Testament longs for it and the prophets foresee it. Jesus announces that it has come near in himself.

entries.title: Judgment and Justice
entries.blurb: Because God is good, he does not ignore evil. He judges nations and individuals in history and will judge the world in righteousness at the end.

entries.blurb: Christian hope is not escape from the body but the resurrection of the body and a renewed creation. Christ's bodily resurrection is the first fruits of it.

entries.keywords: Psalm 95:6

entries.title: The Gift You Cannot Earn
entries.blurb: Grace is getting something good you could never have earned, just because God is generous.
entries.keywords: Ephesians 2:8-9

entries.title: Turning Around
entries.blurb: Repentance is turning around and going the other way, which asks more of you than feeling sorry.

entries.title: Not Getting What You Deserve
entries.blurb: Mercy is choosing kindness when someone has earned the opposite.
entries.keywords: Micah 6:8

entries.title: Whose Voice Gets Heard
entries.blurb: God cares deeply about the people the world forgets, and He wants us to speak up for them.
entries.keywords: Proverbs 31:8-9

entries.title: The Hardest Love
entries.blurb: Anyone can love the people who are nice to them. Jesus calls us to love even the people who aren't.
entries.keywords: Matthew 5:44-45

entries.title: Small but Powerful
entries.blurb: Words are tiny, but they can build people up or burn them down.
entries.keywords: James 3:5

entries.title: The Thief of Glad
entries.blurb: Comparing yourself to others will steal your joy faster than almost anything.
entries.keywords: Galatians 6:4

entries.title: The Right Kind of Awe
entries.blurb: Fearing God means taking Him seriously, with awe, the way you feel small and glad at the edge of the ocean.
entries.keywords: Proverbs 9:10

entries.title: More Than Being Smart
entries.blurb: Being smart is knowing a lot. Being wise is knowing what to do with what you know.
entries.keywords: James 1:5

entries.title: When It Really Hurts
entries.blurb: God does not waste our pain. He can bring good even out of the hard things.
entries.keywords: Romans 8:28

entries.title: Strength in the Waiting
entries.blurb: Waiting on God is its own kind of work, gathering strength for what comes next.
entries.keywords: Isaiah 40:31

entries.title: He Keeps His Word
entries.blurb: God's love does not run out, and His mercy is new every morning.
entries.keywords: Lamentations 3:22-23

entries.title: Dressed for the Day
entries.blurb: There's a real struggle between good and evil, and God gives us everything we need to stand strong.
entries.keywords: Ephesians 6:11

entries.title: What Grows on the Tree
entries.blurb: Good character grows in you when the Spirit is at work, like fruit on a tree.
entries.keywords: Galatians 5:22-23

entries.title: Upside Down Happy
entries.blurb: Jesus says the truly happy people are the opposite of who the world says they are.
entries.keywords: Matthew 5:3-4

entries.title: The One Who Comes Looking
entries.blurb: Jesus is a shepherd who leads us and would die to keep us safe.
entries.keywords: John 10:11

entries.title: The Father Who Runs
entries.blurb: No matter how far you've run from God, He is already looking down the road for you.
entries.keywords: Luke 15:20

entries.title: Everyone You Meet
entries.blurb: Every person you meet carries the image of God, so every person matters.
entries.keywords: Genesis 1:27

entries.title: You Are Not Just a Keeper
entries.blurb: God doesn't just want us to keep the good news to ourselves. He sends us out to share it.
entries.keywords: Matthew 28:19-20

entries.title: When Someone Hurts You
entries.blurb: Forgiving someone means you hand the debt to God instead of making them pay. You are not saying that what they did was okay.
entries.keywords: Colossians 3:13

entries.title: The Cure for a Grumpy Heart
entries.blurb: Thankfulness is choosing to notice the good gifts God has already given, even on a day when plenty is wrong.
entries.keywords: 1 Thessalonians 5:18

entries.title: Talking with God
entries.blurb: Prayer is talking with a Father who loves to hear you, with no magic words and no fancy speech required.
entries.keywords: Matthew 7:7

entries.title: A Light for the Path
entries.blurb: The Bible is how God talks to us. It's a light that shows us the way to go.
entries.keywords: Psalm 119:105

entries.title: Trusting Enough to Obey
entries.blurb: We obey God not to make him love us, but because we trust that he loves us and knows what is best.
entries.keywords: John 14:15

entries.title: Small Things with Great Love
entries.blurb: Kindness is love you can see. It's noticing other people and doing the small good thing.
entries.keywords: Ephesians 4:32

entries.title: A Happiness That Holds
entries.blurb: Joy is deeper than happy feelings. It's a settled gladness that comes from belonging to God, even on hard days.
entries.keywords: Nehemiah 8:10

entries.title: When Your Heart Is Worried
entries.blurb: Jesus gives a peace that doesn't wait for the problems to go away, because it rests on him and not on them.
entries.keywords: John 14:27

entries.title: Three and Yet One
entries.blurb: There's one God who lives forever as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, three persons who have always loved each other.
entries.keywords: Matthew 28:19-20

entries.title: God Called It Good
entries.blurb: The world was spoken into being by a God who meant to make it and called it good.
entries.keywords: Genesis 1:1

entries.title: How It All Went Wrong
entries.blurb: The world is broken because people stopped trusting God and went their own way, and that same pull lives in all of us.
entries.keywords: Genesis 3:6

entries.title: The God Who Keeps His Word
entries.blurb: God always keeps his promises, every single one, no matter how long it takes.
entries.keywords: Joshua 21:45

entries.title: God Came Close
entries.blurb: God did not stay far away. He became one of us, with skin and a heartbeat, so we could know him.
entries.keywords: John 1:14

entries.title: A Glimpse of the Mender
entries.blurb: The miracles of Jesus were small previews of the day he makes everything broken whole again.
entries.keywords: Matthew 11:5

entries.title: He Is Coming Back
entries.blurb: Jesus came once as a baby to save us, and he is coming again as a King to set everything right.
entries.keywords: Acts 1:11

entries.title: Everything New Again
entries.blurb: God is going to make the world new, the way it was always meant to be, rather than throw it away.
entries.keywords: Revelation 21:5

entries.title: Strong Enough to Be Gentle
entries.blurb: Gentleness is strength that chooses to be careful with people.
entries.keywords: Philippians 4:5

entries.title: Good All the Way Through
entries.blurb: Goodness is choosing to do the right thing, again and again, even when no one notices and it would be easier not to.
entries.keywords: Galatians 6:9

entries.title: Keep Going
entries.blurb: Perseverance is keeping on, one step at a time, all the way to the end, when quitting would be easier.
entries.keywords: Hebrews 12:1

entries.title: Taking Care of What Is Not Yours
entries.blurb: Everything we have is really God's, given to us to take care of well, not to use up however we please.
entries.keywords: 1 Corinthians 4:2

entries.title: Where It All Came From
entries.blurb: Moses said this to people who had eaten manna in the desert for forty years, one day's food at a time, and were about to sit down at full tables of their own. The hungry years had tested them.
entries.keywords: Deuteronomy 8:10-14 thanksgiving gratitude family devotion

entries.title: The One Who Came Back
entries.blurb: Leprosy meant living apart from everyone, even your own family. These men could only call to Jesus from a distance. Then, somewhere on the road, their skin was clean.
entries.keywords: Luke 17:14-18 thanksgiving gratitude family devotion

entries.title: Thanks in the Middle of It
entries.blurb: Paul wrote this to a young church that was suffering for following Jesus. He knew how hard things were for them. Look closely at one small word. He says to give thanks in every circumstance.
entries.keywords: 1 Thessalonians 5:16-18 thanksgiving gratitude family devotion

entries.title: The Year the Fig Tree Did Not Bud
entries.blurb: Habakkuk wrote this knowing an army was coming, and the verse before says his whole body shook with fear. No figs, no grapes, no olives, no grain. For a farmer, that is every paycheck gone at once.
entries.keywords: Habakkuk 3:17-18 thanksgiving gratitude family devotion

entries.title: The Guests Who Cannot Pay You Back
entries.blurb: Most of us make guest lists the way Jesus describes: friends, family, people who will ask us back.
entries.keywords: Luke 14:12-14 thanksgiving gratitude family devotion

entries.title: The Empty Chair
entries.blurb: Tomorrow some of us will set the table with a chair missing. Maybe someone died this year, or long ago and it still hurts. Maybe someone is far away, or our family has come apart.
entries.keywords: John 11:32-35 thanksgiving gratitude family devotion

entries.title: His Love Lasts Forever
entries.blurb: Psalm 136 has twenty-six verses, and every one ends the same way: his loving devotion endures forever. Try it at the table today.
entries.keywords: Psalm 136:1-3 thanksgiving gratitude family devotion

entries.title: The Long Wait Begins
entries.blurb: On the worst day in the story, when everything had already broken, God made a promise. Nothing about that afternoon got fixed, and the promise would take thousands of years to come true.
entries.keywords: Genesis 3:15 advent christmas family devotion

entries.title: A Family for the World
entries.blurb: Abram was old and had no children, and God told him his family would bless the whole world. That's a strange thing to promise an old man with an empty house.
entries.keywords: Genesis 12:1-3 advent christmas family devotion

entries.title: God Hears in the Dark
entries.blurb: The people had been slaves for four hundred years. Four hundred years is longer than the United States has existed. For all that time it must have looked like God wasn't listening.
entries.keywords: Exodus 3:7-8 advent christmas family devotion

entries.title: A King Who Lasts
entries.blurb: David was a real king with a real throne, and God told him a son from his line would reign forever. No human king lasts forever. They get old, they fail, they die.
entries.keywords: 2 Samuel 7:12-13 advent christmas family devotion

entries.title: Out of Bethlehem
entries.blurb: Bethlehem was a small town, the kind of place travelers passed through on the way to somewhere bigger. And God circled it on the map hundreds of years early. He doesn't pick the way we pick.
entries.keywords: Micah 5:2 advent christmas family devotion

entries.title: A Child Is Given
entries.blurb: Isaiah said these words seven hundred years before the first Christmas. He had never seen a manger.
entries.keywords: Isaiah 9:6 advent christmas family devotion

entries.title: A Light in Deep Darkness
entries.blurb: Isaiah didn't pretend the darkness wasn't real. He called it deep, he called it shadow, he didn't soften it. That's honest, and we should be honest too. Some seasons are dark.
entries.keywords: Isaiah 9:2 advent christmas family devotion

entries.title: A Branch from a Stump
entries.blurb: A stump is what is left after a tree gets cut down. It looks finished, dead, done. Israel had been cut down to a stump, the old royal family reduced to almost nothing.
entries.keywords: Isaiah 11:1 advent christmas family devotion

entries.title: Comfort My People
entries.blurb: After many hard chapters, God says one word twice. Comfort, comfort. He's not embarrassed to comfort his people.
entries.keywords: Isaiah 40:1-3 advent christmas family devotion

entries.title: The Servant Who Carries It
entries.blurb: This is the strangest promise of Advent. The one who is coming won't just rule, he will suffer. He will carry our pain on his own back. Most of us spend our lives trying to put down what is heavy.
entries.keywords: Isaiah 53:4-5 advent christmas family devotion

entries.title: A New Heart
entries.blurb: Notice what God promised here. He could have promised us better rules, and we would have taken them. He promised new hearts instead, and there's a difference.
entries.keywords: Ezekiel 36:26 advent christmas family devotion

entries.title: How Long, O Lord
entries.blurb: Even in Advent, full of promises, the people of God asked hard questions out loud. How long. Where are you. David put these questions right into a song he sang in worship. That tells us something.
entries.keywords: Psalm 13:1-2 advent christmas family devotion

entries.title: The Messenger Comes First
entries.blurb: Malachi is the last book before a long silence. After he spoke, four hundred years passed with no prophet, no new word. Imagine waiting four hundred years for a sentence to finish.
entries.keywords: Malachi 3:1 advent christmas family devotion

entries.title: An Old Man Hears Good News
entries.blurb: Zechariah and Elizabeth were old and had prayed for a child for years with no answer. They had probably stopped expecting one. Then God answered a prayer they had nearly given up on.
entries.keywords: Luke 1:13 advent christmas family devotion

entries.title: Let It Be
entries.blurb: Mary was young, probably a teenager, and the angel asked her to carry the Son of God, which would turn her whole life upside down. She had every reason to be afraid of what people would say.
entries.keywords: Luke 1:38 advent christmas family devotion

entries.title: The Lowly Lifted
entries.blurb: When Mary found out what God was doing, she didn't sing a quiet little lullaby.
entries.keywords: Luke 1:52-53 advent christmas family devotion

entries.title: Joseph Stays
entries.blurb: Joseph could have walked away, and no one would have blamed him. Instead he stayed, took on a son who wasn't his by blood, and raised the Savior of the world in a carpenter shop.
entries.keywords: Matthew 1:20-21 advent christmas family devotion

entries.title: The Word Was God
entries.blurb: Before Bethlehem, before the manger, before there was a sky to hang stars in, Jesus already was. The baby in the straw was not the beginning of him. He made the trees that the manger was cut from.
entries.keywords: John 1:1-3 advent christmas family devotion

entries.title: The Word Moved In
entries.blurb: God could have saved us from far away, with a wave of his hand. Instead he came and lived among us, in a real town, on a real street, with people who knew his face.
entries.keywords: John 1:14 advent christmas family devotion

entries.title: The Night Before
entries.blurb: On the night before everything changed, a tired couple was walking a hard road because a faraway emperor wanted to count people for taxes.
entries.keywords: Luke 2:1-5 advent christmas family devotion

entries.title: No Room
entries.blurb: The King of the universe was born in a place where animals ate, because no one had a room for him. From his very first night, Jesus knew what it was to be turned away.
entries.keywords: Luke 2:6-7 advent christmas family devotion

entries.title: Good News for Shepherds
entries.blurb: When God announced the most important birth in history, he sent the news past the palace and the temple to shepherds working the night shift in a field. Shepherds were poor, dirty, and looked down on.
entries.keywords: Luke 2:10-11 advent christmas family devotion

entries.title: Mary Treasured It
entries.blurb: After the shepherds left and the noise died down, Mary didn't rush on to the next thing. She held it all quietly and turned it over in her heart.
entries.keywords: Luke 2:19 advent christmas family devotion

entries.title: A Light to Everyone
entries.blurb: Simeon was old and had waited his whole life to see God keep his promise. When he finally held the baby Jesus, he said he could die in peace now.
entries.keywords: Luke 2:30-32 advent christmas family devotion

entries.title: He Is Here
entries.blurb: Today. After Genesis and the garden, after Abraham and David, after Isaiah and the long silence, after Mary and Joseph and the road to Bethlehem, the word is today.
entries.keywords: Luke 2:11 advent christmas family devotion

entries.title: The Wrong Kind of King
entries.blurb: The crowd wanted a king who would ride in on a war horse and throw out the Romans. Jesus came in on a young donkey, slow and humble, the way kings came when they came in peace.
entries.keywords: Matthew 21:8-9 holy week easter palm sunday good friday family devotion

entries.title: Turning Over the Tables
entries.blurb: The temple was supposed to be the one place where anyone could come close to God, and people had turned it into a marketplace where the poor got cheated. Jesus got angry, and his anger was right.
entries.keywords: Matthew 21:12-13 holy week easter palm sunday good friday family devotion

entries.title: The Greatest Command
entries.blurb: People kept trying to trap Jesus with hard questions that week, hoping he would say something they could arrest him for. He kept answering with the truth instead.
entries.keywords: Matthew 22:37-39 holy week easter palm sunday good friday family devotion

entries.title: A Friend Walks Away
entries.blurb: Judas had walked with Jesus for three years. He had seen the miracles, eaten the meals, heard every word. And he sold his friend for a bag of silver.
entries.keywords: Matthew 26:14-16 holy week easter palm sunday good friday family devotion

entries.title: Bread, Cup, and Basin
entries.blurb: On his last night, Jesus took off his outer robe, knelt down, and washed the dirty feet of his friends, a job usually left to the lowest servant.
entries.keywords: John 13:14-15 holy week easter palm sunday good friday family devotion

entries.title: It Is Finished
entries.blurb: This is the hardest day, and we should not rush past it. Jesus, who had done nothing wrong, was nailed to a cross and died. We call it good, which seems strange for a day with so much pain in it.
entries.keywords: John 19:30 holy week easter palm sunday good friday family devotion

entries.title: The Day of Silence
entries.blurb: Saturday is the day nobody talks about much. Jesus was in the tomb, and his friends didn't know yet that Sunday was coming. They only knew their hope was dead and buried behind a stone.
entries.keywords: Matthew 27:59-60 holy week easter palm sunday good friday family devotion

entries.title: He Is Not Here
entries.blurb: The women came to the tomb in the dark, expecting to care for a dead body. Instead they found the stone rolled away and the grave empty. He had risen.
entries.keywords: Matthew 28:5-6 holy week easter palm sunday good friday family devotion

entries.title: Who made you?
entries.blurb: God made me. I am his creature, called into being by the One who is from everlasting to everlasting, and I belong to him before I belong to anyone else.
entries.keywords: Genesis 1:1

entries.title: Is there a God, and how can we know?
entries.blurb: Yes, there is one true and living God, and we know him because he has made himself known in all he has made and most fully in his Word and in his Son.
entries.keywords: Psalm 19:1

entries.title: What is God?
entries.blurb: God is Spirit, infinite, eternal, and unchanging in his being, wisdom, power, holiness, justice, goodness, and truth.
entries.keywords: John 4:24

entries.title: Is God one, or is God three?
entries.blurb: There is one God who exists eternally as three persons, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, each fully God, equal in power and glory, yet one in being.
entries.keywords: Matthew 28:19-20

entries.title: Did God create everything?
entries.blurb: Yes, God created all things visible and invisible out of nothing, by the word of his power, and everything he made was very good.
entries.keywords: Genesis 1:31

entries.title: How did God create human beings?
entries.blurb: God created human beings, male and female, in his own image, forming us from the dust and breathing into us life, so that we alone among his creatures bear his likeness.
entries.keywords: Genesis 1:27

entries.title: What does it mean to be made in God's image?
entries.blurb: To be made in God's image means we were made to know him, to reflect his character, and to rule over and care for his world as those who answer to him.
entries.keywords: Genesis 1:28

entries.title: Why did God make you?
entries.blurb: God made me to glorify him and to enjoy him forever, finding my deepest life in loving and being loved by the One who made me.
entries.keywords: Isaiah 43:7

entries.title: Does God control all that happens?
entries.blurb: Yes, God rules over all things by his wise and holy will, so that nothing happens by chance, and even hard things are held within the purpose of a good Father.
entries.keywords: Ephesians 1:11-12

entries.title: Is God good even when life is hard?
entries.blurb: Yes, God is always good, for his goodness does not depend on our circumstances, and he works even our suffering toward our good and his glory.
entries.keywords: Romans 8:28

entries.title: What does God require of us?
entries.blurb: God requires that we love him with all our heart, soul, mind, and strength, and that we love our neighbor as ourselves.
entries.keywords: Mark 12:30

entries.title: How has God spoken to us?
entries.blurb: God has spoken to us in his written Word, the Bible, which is breathed out by God, true in all it teaches, and sufficient to make us wise for salvation.
entries.keywords: 2 Timothy 3:16-17

entries.title: What is the Bible mainly about?
entries.blurb: The Bible is mainly about God's plan to rescue sinners through Jesus Christ, so that from beginning to end its true subject is the saving love of God.

entries.title: How did sin come into the world?
entries.blurb: Sin came into the world when our first parents, tempted by the serpent, disobeyed God and ate the fruit he had forbidden, breaking trust with the One who had given them everything.
entries.facet: Sin, the Law, and Our Need
entries.keywords: Genesis 3:6

entries.title: What is sin?
entries.blurb: Sin is any failure to love God and others as we should, whether by doing what God forbids or by failing to do what he commands.
entries.facet: Sin, the Law, and Our Need
entries.keywords: 1 John 3:4

entries.title: Did everyone fall into sin?
entries.blurb: Yes, in Adam all of us fell, so that every person is born with a sinful nature and apart from grace turns away from God.
entries.facet: Sin, the Law, and Our Need
entries.keywords: Romans 5:12

entries.title: What has sin done to us?
entries.blurb: Sin has broken our relationship with God, twisted our desires, brought death into the world, and left us guilty and unable to save ourselves.
entries.facet: Sin, the Law, and Our Need
entries.keywords: Isaiah 59:2

entries.title: What is God's law?
entries.blurb: God's law is his good and perfect will for human life, summed up in the Ten Commandments, showing us how to love God and our neighbor.
entries.facet: Sin, the Law, and Our Need
entries.keywords: Exodus 20:1-2

entries.title: What does the law require of us toward God?
entries.blurb: The first table of the law requires that we worship God alone, honor his name, keep no idols, and set apart time to rest in him and remember his works.
entries.facet: Sin, the Law, and Our Need
entries.keywords: Exodus 20:3

entries.title: What does the law require of us toward others?
entries.blurb: The second table of the law requires that we honor our parents, protect life, keep our promises, tell the truth, respect what belongs to others, and refuse to covet.
entries.facet: Sin, the Law, and Our Need
entries.keywords: Exodus 20:12

entries.title: Can we keep God's law perfectly?
entries.blurb: No, because of our sinful nature we cannot keep God's law perfectly, and even our best efforts fall short of his holiness.
entries.facet: Sin, the Law, and Our Need
entries.keywords: Romans 3:23-24

entries.title: Then why did God give us the law?
entries.blurb: God gave the law to show us his holiness, to expose our sin, and to drive us to Christ, who alone kept it perfectly on our behalf.
entries.facet: Sin, the Law, and Our Need
entries.keywords: Galatians 3:24

entries.title: What do our sins deserve?
entries.blurb: Our sins deserve God's righteous judgment, for a holy God cannot overlook evil, and the wages of sin is death.
entries.facet: Sin, the Law, and Our Need
entries.keywords: Romans 6:23

entries.title: Is there any hope for sinners like us?
entries.blurb: Yes, our only hope is in the mercy of God, who in love sent his Son to save sinners, not because we deserved it but because he is gracious.
entries.facet: Sin, the Law, and Our Need
entries.keywords: 1 Timothy 1:15

entries.title: Who is Jesus Christ?
entries.blurb: Jesus Christ is the eternal Son of God, the second person of the Trinity, who became man to save us, fully God and fully man in one person forever.
entries.keywords: John 1:14

entries.title: Why did the Son of God become a man?
entries.blurb: The Son of God became a man so that he might stand in our place, obeying where we failed and bearing the punishment our sin deserved.
entries.keywords: Hebrews 2:17

entries.title: How was Jesus born?
entries.blurb: Jesus was conceived by the Holy Spirit and born of the virgin Mary, truly human yet without the sin we inherit from Adam.
entries.keywords: Luke 1:35

entries.title: What kind of life did Jesus live?
entries.blurb: Jesus lived a life of perfect obedience, loving God and people fully, resisting every temptation, and fulfilling all righteousness on our behalf.
entries.keywords: Hebrews 4:15

entries.title: Why did Jesus have to die?
entries.blurb: Jesus had to die because the penalty for sin is death, and in love he took that penalty in our place, satisfying God's justice and opening the way to God.
entries.keywords: 1 Peter 3:18

entries.title: What happened on the cross?
entries.blurb: On the cross Jesus bore the wrath of God against our sin, was forsaken in our place, and cried out that it is finished, completing the work of our salvation.
entries.keywords: John 19:30

entries.title: Did Jesus stay dead?
entries.blurb: No, on the third day Jesus rose bodily from the grave, conquering death, proving he is the Son of God, and securing the resurrection of all who trust him.
entries.keywords: 1 Corinthians 15:20

entries.title: Where is Jesus now?
entries.blurb: Jesus has ascended into heaven, where he reigns as Lord over all and intercedes for his people as our great High Priest.
entries.keywords: Hebrews 7:25

entries.title: What does it mean that Jesus is Lord?
entries.blurb: To say Jesus is Lord means he holds all authority in heaven and on earth, so that he has the right to rule every part of our lives.
entries.keywords: Matthew 28:18

entries.title: How are we saved?
entries.blurb: We are saved by grace alone, through faith alone, in Christ alone, not by anything we have done but as a free gift from God.
entries.keywords: Ephesians 2:8-9

entries.title: What is grace?
entries.blurb: Grace is the free and undeserved favor of God, by which he gives sinners what they could never earn and forgives what they could never repay.
entries.keywords: Romans 5:8

entries.title: What is faith?
entries.blurb: Faith is trusting in Jesus Christ alone for salvation, resting not on our own works but on his finished work, receiving him as Savior and Lord.
entries.keywords: John 3:16

entries.title: What is repentance?
entries.blurb: Repentance is a change of heart and direction, in which we turn away from sin and turn toward God, grieving our sin and longing to obey him.

entries.title: What is justification?
entries.blurb: Justification is God's act of declaring us righteous in his sight, forgiving all our sins and crediting to us the perfect righteousness of Christ, received by faith.
entries.keywords: Romans 5:1-2

entries.title: Can anything separate us from God's love in Christ?
entries.blurb: No, nothing in all creation can separate us from the love of God in Christ Jesus, for those he saves he holds securely to the end.
entries.keywords: Romans 8:38-39

entries.title: What does Jesus give us besides forgiveness?
entries.blurb: Besides forgiveness, Jesus gives us himself, making us right with God, adopting us as children, and granting us eternal life that begins even now.
entries.keywords: John 10:10

entries.title: Who is the Holy Spirit?
entries.blurb: The Holy Spirit is the third person of the Trinity, fully God, who applies the work of Christ to us, dwells in believers, and gives us life with God.
entries.facet: The Spirit, New Life, the Church, and Last Things
entries.keywords: John 14:26

entries.title: What is the new birth?
entries.blurb: The new birth, or regeneration, is the work of the Holy Spirit by which he gives spiritual life to those who were dead in sin, making them new creations in Christ.
entries.facet: The Spirit, New Life, the Church, and Last Things
entries.keywords: John 3:7

entries.title: What does it mean to be adopted by God?
entries.blurb: To be adopted means God makes us his own children, giving us his name, his care, and a sure place in his family forever.
entries.facet: The Spirit, New Life, the Church, and Last Things
entries.keywords: Galatians 4:6

entries.title: What is sanctification?
entries.blurb: Sanctification is the lifelong work of the Spirit by which we grow to be more like Jesus, putting sin to death and coming alive to righteousness.
entries.facet: The Spirit, New Life, the Church, and Last Things
entries.keywords: Philippians 1:6

entries.title: How does the Spirit change us?
entries.blurb: The Spirit changes us by uniting us to Christ, producing his fruit in us, and giving us the desire and power to obey God from the heart.
entries.facet: The Spirit, New Life, the Church, and Last Things
entries.keywords: Galatians 5:22-23

entries.title: What is the church?
entries.blurb: The church is the whole company of God's people, gathered by the Spirit around Christ, called to worship God, love one another, and make him known to the world.
entries.facet: The Spirit, New Life, the Church, and Last Things
entries.keywords: 1 Peter 2:9

entries.title: What is baptism?
entries.blurb: Baptism is the sign God gives to mark his people, picturing our union with Christ in his death and resurrection and our cleansing from sin.
entries.facet: The Spirit, New Life, the Church, and Last Things
entries.keywords: Romans 6:4

entries.title: What is the Lord's Supper?
